html:
Pashainé (B59) / Empire of Anbennar continuation (Z01)

Region (English survey classification): Empire of Anbennar (EoA).

In one sentence: turn the negotiated politics of the Luna River cities into a state machine, survive a mage takeover crisis, and contest the whole Empire of Anbennar with law, factories and blackpowder.

Story: very high | Mission-tree length: very long (53 B59-campaign-related missions located in the current files, including the Z01 continuation; not added twice) | Mission-tree update: local file modified 2026-07-09, supports v1.37.5.0 | Distinctiveness: very high | Forced waiting/grind: high | Early pressure: medium–high (the Luna River minor-country prologue has its own pressures) | Expansion capacity: very high

A country that does not yet exist

The current localisation identifies this country as Pashainé (B59). It is not a unified country on the 1444 map. Its country-history file's monarchy, Pashainéy culture and capital are a formable-country template, not evidence that every player beginning as a republic automatically becomes a feudal monarchy. What can be established before 1444 is that independent towns and cities line the Luna River, sharing trade, imperial politics and arguments over old Damerian traditions. The offline English Wiki lists Pashainé among potential polities after the 1444 divergence, without a reliable foundation year. Its account of the river cities' earlier guild institutions cannot be projected backwards as proof that B59 already existed.

The four free cities—Menibór, Napesbay, Bluehart and Bellacaire—have their own openings and shared missions, covered separately in the Luna River Four Free Cities collection. Completing their finale gives the most narratively continuous entry into B59, but they are not the only possible founders. Current formation primarily requires appropriate culture, Luna River territory, administrative technology and independence; Luna River minors must additionally complete the finale. A special confederation route can integrate eligible subjects on formation. The decision then changes the Tag to B59 and replaces the non-generic missions. This article therefore starts with the post-formation dedicated mission tree, without counting the four cities' prologue again as Pashainé's 1444 history.

How should a league of cities rule an empire?

Pashainé opens with more than border conquest. It asks whose authority can uphold common rules when guilds, nobles, clergy, mages and citizens disagree. “Standing Side By Side” requires estate loyalty and a courthouse in the capital, while “Torn Identities” describes a good leader as a powerful figure constrained by law, precedent and public morality. Its political writing accepts that politicians bargain and compromise; the virtue of the state must not depend on one individual. The cities' confederal ideal thus develops into a country with central institutions, advisers, an army and imperial ambitions.

It uses the Imperial Chancellorship and parliamentary politics while building urban industry, trade and military supply, expanding into wider Cannor. The official 2025 development diary describes the passage from Luna River unity to imperial power and foreshadows the struggle between mages and the civic state; the release announcement confirms its release with The Final Empire. These are development and publication contexts, not substitutes for current script requirements.

The real rupture is “Prelude To Greatness.” Once the required age, number of cities and country flags are present, greater mage influence and lower loyalty accelerate the disaster. Waiting alone cannot end it: stability must recover and parliament must pass six emergency measures. These address treason, the destruction of mage towers, approved artificery, customs, the army and the security of parliament. Suppressing the mages is not a cost-free justice button: the measures spawn mage rebels and demolish existing towers. At the same time, artificery and steel armaments acquire an institutional place. Only the disaster's end unlocks the later mission line; the player has to complete this restructuring of power.

From B59 to Z01

After the crisis, the missions turn to governance, blackpowder armies, industry and imperial religious politics. “The Dream Lives On” requires substantial development and regional control, then triggers the bespoke “Unity” event: B59 becomes the Empire of Anbennar (Z01) and switches missions. Only a Z01 that was previously B59 and completed the preceding story receives this file's imperial continuation; it is not an ordinary tree shared by every Z01. There is still no single fixed ending. The next event allows “Blackpowder Anbennar” or names and colours appropriate to the government, including the native English “Sovereign State Of Anbennar” and “Republic Of Anbennar.” The former is the English display corresponding to the Chinese article's imperial-monarchical label, not a new Tag. Unification, industry and revolution continue to depend on subsequent missions and player choices.

The local structured database locates 53 missions related to the B59 campaign, including later missions requiring Z01 and a B59 origin. Those Z01-related missions must not be added again, nor can all definitions be assumed visible together in one campaign. Pashainé's long-form appeal lies in this rhythm: manage city-state interests, confront a crisis of mage power, then bring the league's political language into the Empire. Its difficulty follows the same rhythm—formation conditions, estate loyalty, disaster legislation, industrial construction and regional unification take turns blocking progress.

Personality, values and recommendation

The v2.1 coordinates are Expansion 84/100 | Autocracy 61/100 | Magic ↔ Artifice 20/100 (100 = magic, 0 = artifice; theme intensity 82/100) | Pluralism 67/100. Phase profiles shift from Luna River negotiation and pre-crisis mage politics (Expansion 66, Autocracy 42, Magic ↔ Artifice 58) to the post-crisis blackpowder state and imperial unification (Expansion 91, Autocracy 70, Magic ↔ Artifice 8). Early negotiation and mage influence imply more dispersed power and a stronger magical-political presence; later central institutions, artificery and blackpowder armies dominate, hence the separate phase profiles. The state stresses shared citizenship, but there is insufficient evidence to describe equal treatment of every culture and religion as an already implemented institution.

The inherited v2.1 values assessment is Neutral (65/100), with a mixed trajectory. Legal constraints on leaders, urban development and opposition to mage seizure of power support the public good. Treason legislation, tower demolition and armed suppression during the crisis, followed by forceful manipulation of imperial institutions, mean dignity and restraint cannot be rated solely from idealistic declarations. The penalties concern concrete coercive means, not expansion, unification, monarchy or blackpowder technology itself. The crisis's precise victim scope and every branch's in-game outcome remain unverified.

This campaign suits players who enjoy political narrative, city leagues, parliamentary and estate bargaining, blackpowder industry and an exceptionally long imperial second half. If you want uninterrupted conquest after forming a country and do not want to manage six disaster measures and lengthy prerequisites, it can be punishing. Two 2025 player reports praise Luna River influence and the political writing while also complaining about early parliamentary cooldowns and waiting for particular dates. Those are community experiences of their respective versions. Full sources and limits are in the evidence record.

National Ideas (Reference Appendix)

The following reproduces current national traditions, seven national ideas and ambition. Traditions apply on adoption, ideas unlock through investment, and ambition follows completion of all seven. Only national ideas are listed, not racial, governmental or mission bonuses; predecessor and successor sets do not stack. Idea descriptions can recall history or describe future ideals and do not automatically establish events before 1444.

Effect displays and units are inherited for source parity, not independently certified; uncertain percentages remain accompanied by script keys and raw values.

Pashainé (B59) — Pashainéy Ideas

Set ID: B59_ideas. Source: project-verified Mod script (public artifact omits local path and line offsets).

Applicability condition (source script):

    trigger = {
        tag = B59
    }

Pashainéy Traditions

  • Legitimacy: +1 (legitimacy; raw value 1).

  • Devotion: +1 (devotion; raw value 1).

  • Republican tradition: +0.3 (republican_tradition; raw value 0.3).

  • Horde unity: +1 (horde_unity; raw value 1).

  • Trade steering: +20% (trade_steering; raw value 0.2).

1. Friends in High Places

“The greatest rulers preside not over a mere reign but an Era, a period which eclipses those ahead and behind in its profundity and prolificity. They understand that the legacy of the patron is his clients.” Tomás of Vallusna, ‘The Statesman’

  • Estate interaction cooldown modifier: -10% (estate_interaction_cooldown_modifier; raw value -0.1).

  • Administrative advisor cost: -25% (adm_advisor_cost; raw value -0.25).

2. Damerian Renaissance

“The imitation of style necessitates the imitation of form, and therefore of function. When we build a colonnade inspired by the formal markets of Old Dameria, we are inspired also by the conversation held along that colonnade, the type of life enabled by the structure we seek to recreate. The rhetorical tradition, the vibrant public life, even the raucous protest – all are made possible by the decision, made once again, to build space for them.” Saman of Fowlbarn, ‘The Life Of Stone’

  • Monthly splendor: +1 (monthly_splendor; raw value 1).

  • Idea cost: -10% (idea_cost; raw value -0.1).

3. Guild Philosophy

“Even in those realms which had not subordinated their government to an association of guild-backed aldermen, the Guild had been the fundamental unit of urban life in the Eastern Dameshead long before Pashainé’s emergence as a coherent state.

This had three major consequences. First, the codification of a sort of corporate democracy, a belief that society was best forged under a competing set of mutually-exerted pressures, by groups representing collectives of the population - even if these were subject to a monarch or a so-called ’Executive Guild’. Second, an emphasis on economic prosperity, the brass tacks ‘shopkeeper diplomacy’ for which Pashainé became notorious. Third, a relentless focus on urbanisation and the vertical integration of industry.” Silvard Dove, ‘An Economic History of Cannor’

  • Promoted culture development cost: -15% (development_cost_in_primary_culture; raw value -0.15).

4. Blended Identity

“The poet Milian said that the Pashainéy is uniquely noble, having inherited the bravery of his Vernman father and the dignity of his Damerian mother. As a second daughter, I seem to have been left with the libido and stubbornness.” Genaia ‘Geni’ Cadesna sina Bellacaire, ‘Memoirs Of A Fallen Countess’

  • Free policies: +1 (free_policy; raw value 1).

5. Cradle of Ravelianism

“Consider the conflict between Corinism and the Court which had so split the Valley. Consider, then, an unusually literate and engaged populace with a political impetus to see theological ruptures healed. Consider finally the Ravelian Lodge, which in its structure mimics the voluntary association basis of the guild. No population on Halann was more ready to embrace not merely the articles of belief but the basic organisational structure of Ravelianism.” Leande Bellac, ‘Apologetics’

  • Institution spread in true-faith provinces: +20% (institution_spread_from_true_faith; raw value 0.2).

  • Papal influence: +2 (papal_influence; raw value 2).

6. Birthplace of Protest

“Over the course of the eighteenth century, the slowly aggregating impact of the Verdancy became more and more clear across the entire Luna watershed. Land which had once been among the most fertile in Cannor gave harvest perhaps once in two years, while the concomitant soil pollution devastated the Valley’s few remaining natural forests. The result was an exodus of the population from the countryside and an even greater urbanisation of Pashainé, inadvertently birthing a contentious café and street culture; this would dominate the labour politics of the following hundred years, erupting again and again into civil unrest. You will find few along the Valley who have much to say in praise of Camir Silmuna, but our land is indelibly marked by his legacy.” Lucas síl Bellacaire, The History of the Lilac River, Vol. II

  • Army morale: +10% (land_morale; raw value 0.1).

7. Fallen and Remembered

“Do not fear death, my people. Fear nothing which you do in the company of brave souls; fear nothing which you do among your fellow citizens! We live in the time of the Mage-Emperors – in the era of the staff – and its power seems absolute. But we know these mages can die.

We knew it three hundred years ago, when the discipline of the fusillade first began to rival the arc of the fireball. We knew it two hundred years ago, when first we learned of that glorious substance, then accessible only so very far away, which could countermand their unearned gifts. And we know it now – now that their ritual of growth, their promise of endless harvest, has wrought a desolate steppe where once there was only verdant life. It is what they do! Addle the land, poison the water, wreck the bountiful Halann we share for the slightest chance at a lonely throne.

Hear me! It’s true – we may die today. But we die together, while they die alone.” Carric of Paredocks, Final Address

  • Leader land shock: +1 (leader_land_shock; raw value 1).

Pashainéy Ambition

  • National tax modifier: +20% (global_tax_modifier; raw value 0.2).

Menibór (A55) — Menibórian Ideas

Set ID: A55_ideas. Source: project-verified Mod script (public artifact omits local path and line offsets).

Applicability condition (source script):

    trigger = {
        tag = A55
    }

Menibórian Traditions

  • Mercenary Discipline: +5% (mercenary_discipline; raw value 0.05).

  • Trade efficiency: +10% (trade_efficiency; raw value 0.1).

  • May recruit female generals: Allowed (may_recruit_female_generals; raw value yes).

1. City of Valor

Menibór is second only to Anbenncóst itself in terms of how many adventurers hail from our city. From Derwing to Aiscestir, hopeful heroes of the Eastern Dameshead and beyond flock to our inns and taverns to begin their lives as adventurers, forming powerful and prestigious companies such as the Menibór Free Company in the process.

  • Mercenary Maintenance: -20% (merc_maintenance_modifier; raw value -0.2).

  • Mercenary Cost: -20% (mercenary_cost; raw value -0.2).

2. Arcane Wards

During the Wars of Rule, the Magisters of Oldtower and the knights of Valiant Keep frequently clashed near our city, their magics risking the integrity of our walls on several occasions. To deal with them, small anti-magic wards were created to be mounted on the walls and worn by our warriors, allowing them to properly defend Menibór from the arcane chaos spreading around her.

  • shock_damage_received：-10% (shock_damage_received; raw value -0.1).

3. Bridgewine and Boar

Nothing soothes a tired adventurer more than a serving of Bridgewine with a hefty sausage!

Known more professionally as simply 'Menibór', it is a moderately strong red wine that is known for its spicy notes and high acidity - and has found strong favor amongst the bolder characters of Cannor.

  • Production efficiency: +10% (production_efficiency; raw value 0.1).

4. The Free City

Ever since the fall of the Damerian Republic our city has been one that few can manage to hold onto for long. Several times Damerian and Vernman forces alike were banished from the city by the adventurer companies and embroiled in bloody wars to reclaim her. Even though we've settled into the Empire, our neighbors know well the lengths a Menibórian will go to for our continued autonomous status.

  • Army morale: +10% (land_morale; raw value 0.1).

5. In The Loop

The Loop is the most famed tavern in the Luna Basin, only catering to the most legendary heroes, who frequently gather there to discuss happenings and glories abroad. The proprietors of the establishment are quick to inform us of anything of note that they hear, always ensuring the reach of our city council remains in The Loop.

  • Spy network construction: +10% (spy_offence; raw value 0.1).

  • global_spy_defence：+10% (global_spy_defence; raw value 0.1).

6. Riverstone Clan

The dwarves of the Riverstone Clan were hired long ago to construct the many bridges that cross the Luna in our city, and they stayed behind to maintain them. As the city grew around their homes and workshops they expanded their influence, constructing virtually every structure in Menibór and operating as the city's primary architects and engineers to this day.

  • Construction cost: -10% (build_cost; raw value -0.1).

7. Hall of the Gallant

The dream of every adventurer from Menibór is to have their statues and names featured in the hallowed corridors of the Hall of the Gallant, a vast memorial dedicated to those heroes that lost their lives fighting for glory and justice. With names and busts dating back to before the Dragonwake, it is the most well known and respected edifice in the city.

  • Prestige: +1 (prestige; raw value 1).

Menibórian Ambition

  • Republican tradition: +0.3 (republican_tradition; raw value 0.3).

Napesbay (A82) — Napesbayer Ideas

Set ID: A82_ideas. Source: project-verified Mod script (public artifact omits local path and line offsets).

Applicability condition (source script):

    trigger = {
        tag = A82
    }

Napesbayer Traditions

  • Sailor Modifier: +15% (global_sailors_modifier; raw value 0.15).

  • Naval Morale: +10% (naval_morale; raw value 0.1).

1. Vernid Arsenal

To prevent complete Damerian domination of the seas the old kingdom of Verne had established a bustling arsenal in Napesbay. Though the kingdom might've fallen long ago the infrastructure still stands, allowing us to continue producing vessels at a rapid rate, albeit under a different liege.

  • Shipbuilding Time: -20% (global_ship_recruit_speed; raw value -0.2).

  • Ship Cost: -5% (global_ship_cost; raw value -0.05).

2. Brigand's Bane

Pirates of the Damesneck know to steer clear of Napesbayer vessels, for many a villainous corsair has been sent the sea floor by our guns over the centuries.

  • Galley Combat Ability: +10% (galley_power; raw value 0.1).

3. Napesfleet

For centuries Napesbay was the home of the secondary Imperial fleet, frequently referred to as the Napesfleet, mirroring Neckcliffe across the Damesneck. When the Lilac Wars came roaring however, we knew that the fleet would only serve to make us a target should it remain in the hands of the Emperor. Thus, when the order came for the ships to leave port our officials seized the ships, declaring them property of the city and chasing down the ones that attempted to flee. While the Silmuna were understandably upset, bigger problems drew their attention from us and the fleet of Neckcliffe served well in our stead.

For most of the conflict anyway.

  • Naval Force Limit Modifier: +15% (naval_forcelimit_modifier; raw value 0.15).

  • Chance to Capture Enemy Ships: +10% (capture_ship_chance; raw value 0.1).

4. Pírluna Vineyards

Along the gentle and slow-moving Pírluna are vineyards and wineries, tranquil slices of land owned by retired adventurers from Menibór. With a countryside more akin to the estate of a Wine Lord, they're one of the main employers in Napesbay, only after the arsenal and the navy.

  • Goods produced modifier: +10% (global_trade_goods_size_modifier; raw value 0.1).

5. Napesbay Company

Ruben of Napesbay was a daring and dashing captain, who led the colonial efforts of Verne, becoming one of the most famous explorers in Cannor. He of course didn't forget his home city, returning with gold and silver to establish a new colonial trading company in Napesbay, bringing trade from Aelantir back home.

  • Global trade power: +10% (global_trade_power; raw value 0.1).

6. Gems in the Rough

Many of the pirate captains the captains of Napesbay captures are quite skilled, and it would be a waste to not make use of their talents. By establishing a rehabilitation program we can turn these rowdy raiders into proud admirals of the Napesfleet, fighting to finally rid the sea of their former comrades.

  • Naval Leader Fire: +2 (leader_naval_fire; raw value 2).

7. Rise of Napesbay

With the Napesbay Company running well and the Napesfleet keeping the seas clear of piracy, Napesbay has swiftly grown into one of the most prominent ports in the Damesneck. Many of the adventurers and settlers flocking to Aelantir leave Cannor through our city, and countless more have been moving here to establish new businesses, at home and abroad. Truly, this is Napesbay's golden age.

  • Development cost: -10% (development_cost; raw value -0.1).

Napesbayer Ambition

  • Number of merchants: +1 (merchants; raw value 1).

Bluehart (A61) — Blueharter Ideas

Set ID: A61_ideas. Source: project-verified Mod script (public artifact omits local path and line offsets).

Applicability condition (source script):

    trigger = {
        tag = A61
    }

Blueharter Traditions

  • Diplomatic reputation: +200% (diplomatic_reputation; raw value 2).

  • Development cost: -10% (development_cost; raw value -0.1).

1. Tempering Ambition

Bluehart has always been surrounded by ambitious lords, eager to feast upon the riches of the Luna. Many a would-be conqueror have been turned away from our city, though not through the sword, but through the power of words. Our officials are experts in negotiating peace and reconciliation even with the most belligerent warlords, keeping our people safe from the horrors of combat.

  • Improve relations: +20% (improve_relation_modifier; raw value 0.2).

2. Legacy of the Hartlord

Our city was originally founded as a legionary camp of the 21st Legion of Dameria, also known as the Legion XXI Hart. When the Republic fell to the Dragonwake, the former commander took control of the situation, allowing panicked civilians to flock to his protection and enforcing stability across the suddenly lawless frontier. In time he became known as The Hartlord, a paragon of peace and law, and when the Kingdom of Dameria rose from the ashes of the Republic, he readily submitted the new city of Bluehart to their rule, dying in his sleep as peacefully as he reigned. We hope to continue his legacy, acting as a force for goodwill despite whatever horrors wrack the lands around us.

  • Stability cost modifier: -15% (stability_cost_modifier; raw value -0.15).

3. Heart of the Luna

With the exception of Port Munas, our city is the largest on the Luna River. A prime destination for trade flowing downstream from the Wexhills, Blueharter merchants have little trouble finding markets to trade with from the comfort of home.

  • Global trade power: +10% (global_trade_power; raw value 0.1).

4. Cymcestir

The old legion camp is known as the Cymcestir, though it hasn't been used for its original wartime purposes for quite some time. Ever since the reign of The Hartlord, the compound has been used as a diplomatic complex, providing comforting accommodations for foreign dignitaries and secure rooms for tense negotiations.

  • Diplomatic relations: +1 (diplomatic_upkeep; raw value 1).

5. Sons of the XXI

Each member tracing direct lineage to the soldiers of the Legion XXI Hart, the Sons of the XXI are the brave sentinels of Bluehart, they alone are permitted to bear arms within city limits. They're said to fight with the ferocity of ten men each, determined to safeguard the city their ancestors fought for, that their children will grow up in, and that their descendants will continue to defend.

  • Infantry combat ability: +10% (infantry_power; raw value 0.1).

6. City of Tranquility

While turmoil brews around the city, none reaches past our city gates. Within the city is an atmosphere of tranquility, largely untouched by whatever calamity plagues the rest of the Empire.

  • National unrest: -2 (global_unrest; raw value -2).

7. Olóiegéanur Academy

The Cymcestir was expanded and converted into the Olóiegéanur Academy in 1604 as a result of simmering tensions within the fabric of Anbennar. The professors of the establishment find great gratification in training the next generation of statesmen and emissaries to act as agents of peace, ready to mend broke bridges across the Empire and assist in healing the wounds of the past.

  • Diplomats: +1 (diplomats; raw value 1).

Blueharter Ambition

  • National tax modifier: +10% (global_tax_modifier; raw value 0.1).

Bellacaire (Z03) — Bellacairey Ideas

Set ID: Z03_ideas. Source: project-verified Mod script (public artifact omits local path and line offsets).

Applicability condition (source script):

    trigger = {
        tag = Z03
    }

Bellacairey Traditions

  • Fort maintenance: -15% (fort_maintenance_modifier; raw value -0.15).

  • Production efficiency: +10% (production_efficiency; raw value 0.1).

1. Bellac's Rock

The most unique and storied structure of Bellacaire is the looming fortress of Bellac's Rock, first built by the King of Verne, Bellac Vernid, in 587 AA as a border fortress against Dameria. For centuries it stood against the ambitions of the north, up until it was seized from the Vernids in 917 AA, acting as a bastion against her original owners until it came under siege and occupation during the War of the Sorcerer-King. Despite its long and tumultuous history, Bellac's Rock is as sturdy as ever, a mighty citadel that continues to guard the lands around it.

  • Fort defense: +20% (defensiveness; raw value 0.2).

2. Free City Confederation

When the winds of war blew across the Upper Luna, Bellacaire organized a neutrality pact with her fellow Free Cities of the river. Though it was ultimately short lived, the brief moment of unity along the Luna is a goal every Bellacairey hopes to replicate, to forge a realm strong enough to protect itself from being pulled into the conflicts of others.

  • Stability cost modifier: -15% (stability_cost_modifier; raw value -0.15).

3. Battle of the Salt and Lance

Despite our city's declared neutrality in the Lilac Wars, in the final days of the conflict she became the site of a brutal, yet inspiring, battle. The treacherous Cestiranders, recently supporters of the Rose Party, charged towards the city while the Galéinni did the same, both powers seeking to seize Bellacaire for their own ambitions. They met outside our gates, clashing in bloody melee while our own warriors took the field to defend the city. After four days and three nights, the invading forces were both forced to withdraw, for the guard of Bellacaire had ensured she would continue to stand free.

  • Army morale: +10% (land_morale; raw value 0.1).

  • Prestige: +0.5 (prestige; raw value 0.5).

4. Lunawalk

Running along the Luna River, the Lunawalk is where most Damerians settled after the fall of Bellac's Rock, establishing a patrician district along the gentle and serene banks. Far from reach of the great shadow cast by the Rock and gently lit by the moon at night, it is the most prestigious neighborhood in the city.

  • Prestige decay: -1% (prestige_decay; raw value -0.01).

5. The Drabsburd

On the other side of the city, far from the opulent abodes of the Lunawalk, the workshops and laboratories of the Drabsburd buzz and churn night and day. The strange gadgets and trinkets produced by the gnomes of the district are awe-inspiring to the populace, and the city government largely leaves the gnomes to innovate and invent at will, so long as they enforce safe practices and procedures.

  • Innovativeness gain: +0.5 (innovativeness_gain; raw value 0.5).

  • Idea cost: -10% (idea_cost; raw value -0.1).

6. Impartial in Heavens and Halann

In the end, it truly doesn't matter who rests upon the throne of the Regent Court, for all of us shall know for sure when we pass from this world. Here one can find Adeanics and Corinites living in peace, free from the dogmatic hatred that drives their religious compatriots to battle outside the city.

  • Tolerance of heretics: +2 (tolerance_heretic; raw value 2).

7. Pink Stripe

The horrors of the war between the Corinite and Adeanic Leagues has left countless refugees and orphans in its wake, and the majority of the Empire is content to let them suffer in silence. This will not stand for us. The Pink Stripe is an organization based in Bellacaire to assist and nurture those devastated by war and disaster, regardless of creed, allegiance, race, or otherwise. Already they've established charters across Anbennar, looking after those that have been left behind.

  • Diplomatic reputation: +200% (diplomatic_reputation; raw value 2).

Bellacairey Ambition

  • Garrison size: +0.3 (garrison_size; raw value 0.3).

Empire of Anbennar (Z01) — Blackpowder Ideas

Set ID: Z01_blackpowder_ideas. Source: project-verified Mod script (public artifact omits local path and line offsets).

Applicability condition (source script):

    trigger = {
        tag = Z01 #Empire of Anbennar
        has_country_flag = anbennar_blackpowder
    }

Blackpowder Traditions

  • morale_damage_received：-10% (morale_damage_received; raw value -0.1).

  • Maximum general fire: +1 (max_general_fire; raw value 1).

1. The Blackpowder War

No other state has so directly confronted the spectre of magical autocracy as our own. The perennial threat of the Witch-King has haunted Cannor for a thousand years, and only we have proven resolute enough to confront this inevitably recurring danger. The result? A state which defends its people, which stands against the conniving, seditious chatter of the scholar’s den. Our association with blackpowder is well-earned, for it is by the miracle of the citizen’s firearm that we have finally drawn equal with the mage, and out of the barrel of the rifle that we have finally made the humble safe.

  • Land fire damage: +20% (fire_damage; raw value 0.2).

2. Silver and Steel

Amongst an assembled crowd of dignitaries from all of Cannor, attended by their loyal supporters and victorious generals, the emperor of the now centralized Anbennar delivered a speech in the Grand Ballroom of the Silver Moon, which had been redecorated for the occasion: the proclamation of a truly united Empire. He told them that the future of Anbennar would be decided by silver and steel.

A colorful sea of faces squinted and pursed their lips - the future? The Emperor spoke as if the great task was still ahead, not behind them. What could he mean? It was a simple yet effective rhetorical gambit - the curious audience listened in rapt attention as the Emperor expounded on the meaning of their words.

Silver is the Empire's color, of its banners, of its coinage, of its diplomacy. Silver for the moon, or perhaps for Castellos. The influence of the half-elven Silver Families runs deep, as does, of course, their blood descent. The memory of the heroic Silver Band that expelled the Sorcerer-King lives on in song and story. Silver arms kept evil at bay, and silver tongues brought the imperial princes together.

Steel is simpler. Steel for the spears of Verne, for the muskets of the Vanbury Guild, for the guns of Giberd. Steel from the foundries of Telgeir and the forge of Anvilwright. The lessons of half a hundred different military traditions and industrial practices will power the Empire's march into the future.

1. The Mages' Peace

The Empire of Anbennar was first established at the Grand Summit of Aranthíl in 1221 AA.

For a small group of like-minded mages and their supporters among the Cannorian nobility, the time of secrecy had ended. They declared their leader, Delian Whitecloak, the first Emperor of Anbennar. The lands around the Dameshead had known naught but war and chaos for decades, even centuries - some elven warriors hadn't seen a lasting peace since their arrival in Cannor. Delian Whitecloak and his compatriots envisioned an end to the endless conflict, brought about through a force that could cut through any king, any army: magic.

The Interregnum lasted sixty years. In six months, it was over. From Vertesk to Verne, from Beepeck to Bennon, warlords set aside their differences and their long standing feuds in the name of unity. Many had to be compelled to do so, through domination or destruction, but in the end they all welcomed the new peace.

Since then, mages have held incalculable influence over the Empire's affairs. Only a mage could sit the Dove Throne. Magical ability was a requirement for legitimate succession. Even when the regime of Mage-Emperors came to an end during the Wars of Rule, they were replaced by the Magisterium, which ruled over the institutions of magic throughout much of Cannor, and controlled an Imperial electorate for centuries. While that influence has waxed and waned over the years, the notion that extraordinary abilities wielded by extraordinary people can change the world has remained.

Anbennar, arise! There will be peace once again.

2. Silver and Steel

Amongst an assembled crowd of dignitaries from all of Cannor, attended by their loyal supporters and victorious generals, the emperor of the now centralized Anbennar delivered a speech in the Grand Ballroom of the Silver Moon, which had been redecorated for the occasion: the proclamation of a truly united Empire. He told them that the future of Anbennar would be decided by silver and steel.

A colorful sea of faces squinted and pursed their lips - the future? The Emperor spoke as if the great task was still ahead, not behind them. What could he mean? It was a simple yet effective rhetorical gambit - the curious audience listened in rapt attention as the Emperor expounded on the meaning of their words.

Silver is the Empire's color, of its banners, of its coinage, of its diplomacy. Silver for the moon, or perhaps for Castellos. The influence of the half-elven Silver Families runs deep, as does, of course, their blood descent. The memory of the heroic Silver Band that expelled the Sorcerer-King lives on in song and story. Silver arms kept evil at bay, and silver tongues brought the imperial princes together.

Steel is simpler. Steel for the spears of Verne, for the muskets of the Vanbury Guild, for the guns of Giberd. Steel from the foundries of Telgeir and the forge of Anvilwright. The lessons of half a hundred different military traditions and industrial practices will power the Empire's march into the future.

5. One Crown

The end of the Fourth Lilac War in 1443 saw the Empire in a sorry state, fraying at the edges as Lorent, Gawed, and Ibevar picked at the borders. Soldiers of Emperor Lothane III marched through the capital of Anbenncóst, not in glory, but amidst flames, and carrying away loot. The Rose and Moon Parties licked their wounds and sharpened their daggers, and the Electors all but openly disregarded the emperor's will; Lothane III may have been a terror on the battlefield, but he was an old man, a Wexonard without silver lineage, with only a human's lifespan. Another, stronger and wiser, or maybe one more willing to "forgive" and "compromise", would soon come into the Dove Throne. After all, the success of a great man - or woman - with the will to dominate and restructure the Empire would come at the expense of the Empire's privileged princes. And if worst came to worst, the princes could always call upon Crothán to furnish a 'legal scholar' to defend their rights in the Imperial Court for a couple of decades.

Nonetheless, the Empire - with some considerable help from a certain faction - pulled itself together. The smaller states agreed to a new model of centralization that would protect them from the depredations of their larger neighbors. A common tax was levied for the first time in centuries. The Imperial Parliament was consolidated and streamlined into a functional legislature, with a permanent session. The Imperial Estates and the Prince-Electors were brought to heel, and with the revocation of the Privilege Against Appeal, the Emperor was once again the supreme authority of the realm. And who could possibly dissent? It was either the petty strife of individual, independent princes... Or a single nation, with purpose indivisible, capitulating only to the Dove Throne.
